items.title: Can LLMs Actually Do Things? (Not Just Talk)
items.summary:
CME295 Transformers and Large Language Models is open for enrollment until September 6. Learn more: https://online.stanford.edu/courses/cme295-transformers-and-large-language-models

LLMs can understand and generate text. But can they actually do things — plan, use tools, adapt when a step fails?

Stanford Adjunct Professors Shervine and Afshine Amidi explain what actually makes an AI system an "agent," presenting the open question: how do you evaluate whether one is working?

#AIAgents #LLM #Transformers #StanfordOnline #AI #MachineLearning #Shorts

items.title: New Stanford Course: Agentic AI
items.summary:
The people who trained PaLM and Gemini are teaching you to build AI agents.

Our Agentic AI course brings you the same graduate curriculum taught on campus in CS329A, adapted for working professionals. 

Your instructors:
Dr. Aakanksha Chowdhery, Adjunct Professor, Stanford Engineering: led end-to-end training of the 540B PaLM model, the largest densely trained language model in the world at the time, and drove pre-training and scaling of Gemini's mixture-of-experts models.

Azalia Mirhoseini, Assistant Professor of Computer Science, Stanford: co-developed the MoE architectures now used in nearly every frontier model, created AlphaChip (the RL method behind Google's TPU designs), and pioneered LLM test-time scaling. She worked on both Claude and Gemini.

What you'll learn:
• Design agentic systems for complex, multi-step real-world tasks
• Apply test-time scaling to boost LLM performance
• Use self-improvement methods like verifiers, feedback loops, RL, and search
• Build agents that use tools and take actions effectively
• Add retrieval, long-term memory, and multi-step planning
• Evaluate agent performance with robust frameworks

Included: 90 days of access, optional live sessions every six weeks with guest speakers and course facilitators, a peer discussion forum, and coding assignments. Conclude the course by building a small-scale AI agent.

items.title: Post-Training Techniques: How LLMs Learn to Follow Instructions
items.summary:
CME295 Transformers and Large Language Models is open for enrollment until September 6. Learn more: https://online.stanford.edu/courses/cme295-transformers-and-large-language-models

A pretrained LLM is good at predicting text — but that's not the same as following instructions well. Stanford Adjunct Professors Shervine and Afshine Amidi walk through the techniques that close that gap: fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, preference optimization, verifier-guided training, and distillation.

CME296 Diffusion and Large Vision Models will be available in Spring 2027. Learn more about that course here: https://online.stanford.edu/courses/cme296-diffusion-and-large-vision-models

#PostTraining #LLM #Transformers #AI #MachineLearning #ReinforcementLearning #OnlineCourses

items.title: Agentic AI Program Overview
items.summary:
Learn more: https://stanford.io/4iHlGQp

Build modern AI agents with Stanford's graduate-level curriculum, adapted for working professionals.

Taught by Stanford Adjunct Professor Chowdhery and Assistant Professor Mirhoseini, this Agentic AI program takes you beyond basic LLM prompting to agents that reason, plan, use tools, and improve themselves through interaction with their environment.

What you'll learn:
- Design agentic systems for complex, multi-step real-world tasks
- Apply test-time scaling to boost LLM performance
- Use self-improvement methods: verifiers, feedback loops, RL, and search
- Build agents that use tools and take actions effectively
- Add retrieval and long-term memory to LLMs
- Develop planning and multi-step reasoning
- Evaluate agent performance with robust frameworks

Drawing on Stanford research and the latest advances in the field.

About the Instructors
Stanford Engineering Adjunct Professor Dr. Aakanksha Chowdhery led end-to-end training of the 540B PaLM model (the largest densely trained language model in the world at the time) and drove pre-training and scaling of Gemini's mixture-of-experts models. Stanford Assistant Professor Azalia Mirhoseini co-developed the MoE architectures now used in nearly every frontier model, created AlphaChip (the RL method behind Google's TPU designs), and pioneered LLM test-time scaling; she worked on both Claude and Gemini.

items.title: Next-Generation #Energy Storage: From #Batteries to #Grid Solutions
items.summary:
Check out Matt and Yi's online course: https://online.stanford.edu/courses/xeiet215-next-generation-energy-storage-batteries-grid-solutions?utm_medium=Video&utm_term&utm_campaign=XEIET215&utm_source=Youtube

The grid is changing fast. Renewables are scaling. AI is driving massive new electricity demand. Energy storage is the technology that connects it all.

In our new course, you'll break down the energy storage landscape so you can understand what's real, what's next, and what matters most when choosing a solution.

You'll cover the science, technology, and real-world use-cases for:
- The fundamental principles of energy
- Mechanical and thermal energy storage
- Energy storage as fuel
- Battery fundamentals
- Lithium-ion batteries
- Alternative battery chemistries and technologies

items.title: Course Overview: Next-Generation Battery Storage
items.summary:
Check out Matt and Yi's online course: https://online.stanford.edu/courses/xeiet215-next-generation-energy-storage-batteries-grid-solutions?utm_medium=Video&utm_term&utm_campaign=XEIET215&utm_source=Youtube

Energy storage is fundamentally reshaping global power systems. As renewables scale and electricity demand grows, including from AI data centers, the question is no longer if we need energy storage. It is which technologies, where, and how fast.

In this course, you will break down the energy storage landscape and learn how to evaluate real options for powering the world around the clock, from grid scale systems to advanced batteries.

You'll cover the science, technology, and real-world use-cases for:
- The fundamental principles of energy
- Mechanical, thermal, and electro-chemical energy storage technologies
- Energy storage as fuel
- Battery fundamentals
- Lithium-ion batteries
- Alternative battery chemistries and technologies

items.title: LLMs Don't Have to Write One Word at a Time
items.summary:
CME295 Transformers and Large Language Models is open for enrollment until September 6. Learn more:
https://online.stanford.edu/courses/cme295-transformers-and-large-language-models

Every LLM you've used generates text one word at a time. But what if it didn't?

Stanford Adjunct Professors Shervine and Afshine Amidi break down diffusion LLMs — models that generate text more like an image diffusion model, refining the whole output progressively instead of token-by-token.

items.title: Course Overview - Business Opportunities and Applications of Generative AI
items.summary:
Learn more and enroll in the course: https://online.stanford.edu/courses/xfm111-business-opportunities-and-applications-generative-ai

Generative AI has unlocked incredible opportunities for businesses and organizations. To fully leverage these possibilities and drive innovation, leaders must have a strong understanding of generative AI and its abilities. After completing this course, you will have the skills and knowledge necessary to navigate the AI landscape and harness this powerful technology.

We have gathered some of the most distinguished experts in the field to bring you a conference-style learning experience exploring capabilities, limitations, strategy, innovation, deployment, applications, and the legal implications of generative AI. Developed in collaboration with the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence (HAI), this course will enable you to plan, execute, and use generative AI to improve performance while ensuring the human perspective remains at the forefront.

- Analyze the capabilities and limitations of generative AI within an organizational context.
- Identify opportunities for innovation and execute a successful generative AI strategy.
- Utilize data and AI to improve people management and managerial decision-making.
- Support successful frontline transformation and skill-development in AI-augmented workforces and organizations.
- Explore different types of generative AI agents and their emerging applications in business.
- Analyze the impact of AI on productivity and discuss the economic complexities of integrating AI into the workforce.
- Apply practical techniques for driving human-AI collaboration and productivity in the workplace.
- Evaluate the legal risks of generative AI and their implications for organizations.

Learn details about the Generative AI: Technology, Business, and Society Program: 
https://online.stanford.edu/programs/generative-ai-technology-business-and-society-program

items.title: When AI Stops Being a Project: Turning Technology into Real Value for Patients and Providers
items.summary:
Learn more about Stanford's online Healthcare AI programs: https://stanford.io/3NEt7uE
Check out the AI in Healthcare series playlist:https://stanford.io/3NEt7uE

Matt Lungren, Stanford University - https://profiles.stanford.edu/matthew-lungren
Justin Norden, Stanford University - https://profiles.stanford.edu/justin-norden

Guest speaker: Sandeep Dadlani,  Optum Insight CEO

A fast-paced Stanford Healthcare AI podcast episode with Optum Insight CEO Sandeep Dadlani exploring how large healthcare enterprises are actually using AI today. The conversation covers the shift from simple chatbots to long-running agentic workflows, the exploding costs and risks of LLM tokens, model choice and “lock-in” (including GLM 5.2), and why AI is rapidly becoming the business, not just a project. With candid stories from UnitedHealth Group’s internal AI “harness,” governance, and leadership rituals, this episode is a playbook for health systems and payers trying to move from pilots to real, scaled impact.

items.title: Stanford AA203 Optimal and Learning-Based Control | Spring 2026 | Lecture 19: Model-Based RL
items.summary:
Lecture 19 — Model-based Reinforcement Learning and Conclusions

Read the companion textbook, Principles of Robot Autonomy, free online: https://porabook.com 

To learn more about enrolling in AA203 Optimal and Learning-Based Control, visit: https://online.stanford.edu/courses/aa203-optimal-and-learning-based-control 

Follow along with the course schedule and syllabus: https://stanfordasl.github.io/aa203/sp2526/ 

Lecture slides: https://stanfordasl.github.io/aa203/sp2526/pdfs/lecture/lecture_4.pdf 

Speaker: Dr. Daniele Gammelli

Bio: Dr. Daniele Gammelli is the Research Director of the Machine Intelligence for Robot Autonomy Laboratory at the Italian Institute of Artificial Intelligence (AI4I), and a Researcher in the Department of Aeronautics and Astronautics at Stanford University. Since 2022, he has been a Research Fellow at the Center for Aerospace Autonomy Research (CAESAR) at Stanford and, until 2025, at the Center for Automotive Research at Stanford (CARS). He received his Ph.D. in Machine Learning and Mathematical Optimization from the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) in 2022, where his doctoral thesis was nominated for the DTU Best Thesis of the Year Award and the DTU Young Researcher Award. Dr. Gammelli’s research focuses on developing the algorithmic foundations and system-level methodologies that enable AI-powered autonomous systems to operate safely, efficiently, and reliably in high-stakes environments, with an emphasis on aerospace autonomy and next-generation mobility systems.

Instructors: 
Prof. Marco Pavone, Associate Professor of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Director of Autonomous Vehicle Research at NVIDIA

Dr. Daniele Gammelli, Research Director at the Italian Institute of Artificial Intelligence (AI4I), Researcher at the Department of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Stanford University

Full playlist: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLa9dmHsLK9dg
